posts.caption:
“Text me when you get home.” We’ve been saying it to each other for years. 

So many of us have been carrying this story around all week, checking on each other the way we always have.

Immense gratitude and deep respect to the student journalists at the Cornell Daily Sun, who kept reporting until the rest of the world paid attention.

If this is sitting heavy, RAINN is free, confidential and open 24/7: call 800-656-HOPE, text HOPE to 64673, or chat at rainn.org/hotline. 💛

It all started with a, “Hey babe, can I use a little section of our yard for some flowers?” 😂

Here’s a little timeline of what it’s taken to get us to today! We have flowers coming out of our ears and only a small bit of time before our first frost comes to claim them but it has been worth every single minute! ❤️

Gardening in northern Minnesota is not for the faint of heart, but I’ll be darned because these blooms sure bring a lot of joy!

I am so happy! 💛 That’s the post. 

Tell me one thing you’re grateful for right now!
C’mon, don’t be shy! Hit me with gratitude!

I didn’t expect one cute lil page to change my days this much. 🙃

The checking used to follow me everywhere. Now it lives on my own cute page, and my head finally gets to go do something else, which it turns out it had been waiting years to do.

That’s the whole idea behind my friend Callan’s AI Bootcamp. You look at your week, find the jobs that never needed you in the first place, and build something to hold them so the time comes back to you. 

This dashboard is just one tiny one that I’ve built. The bootcamp is three live sessions starting on September 28!

➡️ Comment BOOTCAMP and I’ll send you the link to get yours, and the dashboard bonus comes with it.

If you need me, I’ll be right here until the first frost 🌺 Swipe to see where we started.

This dahlia garden has been such an adventure, and I can’t even express the joy I feel when I look out the window and see a field of blooms looking back at me.

We’ve been giving flowers away every chance we get (friends, family, even our UPS guy), and the girls have been learning entrepreneurship through their farm stand.

We figured out that dad holding a sign that says “Your wife needs flowers” is a clutch move on a Sunday after football, talk about marketing.

And me? I’ve been learning more about myself the more I learn about this land.

In a few weeks I’ll dig every tuber up to celebrate a successful season, and the best part is they multiply underground, so we’ll divide them, tuck them in for winter, and come spring we’ll have even more to plant and even more to give away.

Everything here is cyclical, and I love that this cycle ends with more than it started with. Dirt under my nails, happiness in my heart 💛

She said it over pizza, and it brought me right back, ten years later. 🥺

Most of us do this quietly, nodding along at baby showers and saying we’re fine, and I did it too. 

I lost two pregnancies back to back before my first daughter, and what I remember most clearly now isn’t the loss itself, it’s how badly I wanted somebody to say it out loud for me when I had no words of my own yet.

There’s no right way through this and no bow at the end of it. Some of us get our babies and some of us build entirely different lives, and both of those women deserve to be spoken for.

So these are the words, if you need them. Send this to the person who doesn’t understand what it feels like, or post it and let it say what you can’t.

If you’re in this club, leave a heart. You don’t have to say anything else, and you don’t have to explain. I just want you to scroll the comments and see how many of us are standing here with you. 💛

And if you do have words, tell me the one thing you wish somebody had said to you back then.

➡️ Comment BIOHACK for every link and my codes to save on the tools I swear by (and have been using for years)

I am in the best shape of my life at 38 and these are the tools that got me here. Just the things I actually use every daily that have changed how I feel in my body. 💪🏼

Life lately: how do you sum up the end of summer? 🥲

Lake swims. Flower stands. An orchard planted. Harvests reaped. Time with family. Enjoying our beautiful city in every possible way, and the weather we wait for all year round. 

Hands in the soil instead of on screens. Drew cleaning up the hive after a bear got into it because no, it wasn’t all sunshine, but it was mostly sunshine. ☀️ 

This is our first back-to-school season where our girls aren’t standing on the front porch with their backpacks on.

The truth is that life offline is so full I forget to come update you, and some of it feels too sacred and special to share, at least for now. 🙃

We’re busy, we’re making moves, but the good kind, the chosen kind. Life is even more different than I expected even a few months ago and it’s so good.

More soon, though if this summer is any indication, probably not thaaaaatttt soon. 😉

Not pictured: our beautiful growing girls, who were there for every single piece of this. (I had to dig through the camera roll to find the ones without them in it.) 💛

Not on my bingo card for this life: becoming a woman who sells flowers off a table on the side of the road and being completely obsessed with it. 🙃

We put 300 tubers in the ground this spring not knowing if a single one would show up, and we had visions for what this could turn into, but none of them come close to watching a car actually slow down and pull over so someone can pick out a bouquet that we grew and cut ourselves. 

My girls are learning how to sell something they grew and what it feels like to have their own money to save, and I’m not sure I could teach them that anywhere else. 🌸

I’ve built a lot of things on the internet and none of them feel like handing someone a bouquet you grew out of your own dirt. 💛

BIG (LIFE) ANNOUNCEMENT and I’ll be honest, I am still not over it. 😱

It took me a hot minute to work out how to say this, so I made eleven slides instead.

Give it to us. Help us make this next chapter our favorite one yet. Tell me everything! 💛

PSA I didn’t know I owed you: my hair is brown. Has been. Apparently I’ve been out here living a whole brunette life offline while half of you were still picturing a blonde, and oh, the nerve of me. 🤣

After the fifth friend this weekend went “wait, your hair is BROWN?!” I figured I’d better post it so it’s real, because that’s evidently how this works now.

I dyed it so long ago I forgot it was ever news, and it turns out God didn’t mess up with the color he handed me the first time, or with yours. Back to my roots in more ways than one! 💛

Comment: PROMPT and I’ll send you the Google doc filled with my exact prompts! 👋 

I have apparently been talking about AI all weekend, which I did not fully register until I walked into a room where four laptops were open and nobody was pretending to do anything else. 😂

The part I keep thinking about is that none of them wanted me to do it for them. They wanted to see what I was typing in, which is a completely different question than the one people were asking a year ago.

There are six prompts, yours entirely free, and they work on the free versions. 

➡️ Comment: PROMPT and the link to the doc is yours. 💛
